statements.status_notes: Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

The covered package builds prevent a failed direct-buffer gzwrite from leaving a caller-owned input pointer available to gzprintf or gzvprintf. They either guard the later formatting entry points or include the pointer-state reset from upstream commit https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148 in the equivalent zlib 1.3.1 error branch. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85091.
Upstream patch ba829a458576d1ff0f26fc7230c6de816d1f6a77 applied. Adds negative length checks in crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 to prevent CPU consumption from infinite loops.
